items.title: Excel exports replace existing workbooks without confirmation

findings.title: Excel exports replace existing workbooks without confirmation
findings.explanation: The TAC save handler passes the chosen directory and default patient-based filename directly to this writer without checking for an existing file (lines 25647–25652 and 25749–25752). A repeated save or same-name patient can therefore destroy a previous workbook without warning; the other Excel save helpers should also be checked.
findings.suggestion: Confirm existing-file replacement, use unique study-aware names, and write safely via a temporary file.

gpt.reason: DynamicPET/qSlicerDynamicPETModuleWidget.cxx:23833-23838 sets the default from the patient name: `d->fileexcel->setText(name + QStringLiteral("_TAC.xlsx"));`. Lines 25647-25652 construct the path from directory and filename, and 25749-25752 pass it directly to the writer. Line 9301 is `    with pd.ExcelWriter(filepath, engine="xlsxwriter") as writer:`: the default write mode replaces an existing workbook, with no overwrite check in the handler. Repeated saves or different studies sharing a patient name can destroy prior results. The other four handlers at 25763-25840 and writers at 9704, 9742, 9799, and 9839 follow the same pattern. Require confirmation or a unique filename and safe replacement.

gemini.reason: Checked DynamicPET/qSlicerDynamicPETModuleWidget.cxx lines 9291-9313, 9688-9715, 9717-9745, and 25647-25849. The Excel save button handlers construct `fullPath = QDir(path).filePath(filename)` from the UI directory selector and filename text box (which defaults to a patient-based filename) and call `pd.ExcelWriter(filepath, engine="xlsxwriter")`, which overwrites an existing file at that path without a confirmation dialog. However, writing directly to the user-specified directory and filename when the user clicks the Save button is a standard UI/UX omission (lack of an overwrite prompt), not a blocking safety issue.

items.title: Parametric-map export silently deletes existing files

findings.title: Parametric-map export silently deletes existing files
findings.evidence:
output_path = os.path.abspath(str(output_path))
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_path), exist_ok=True)
        if os.path.isfile(output_path):
            os.remove(output_path)

        pm.save_as(output_path, enforce_file_format=True)
findings.explanation: When DICOM output is selected, the caller constructs deterministic filenames from the patient name, model and field (lines 22185–22205). Repeating an export into the same directory, including for a different study of the same patient, silently deletes the previous map; if writing fails after removal, the previous file is already lost.
findings.suggestion: Detect collisions before export, ask for explicit replacement or generate unique filenames, and write to a temporary file before an atomic replacement.

gpt.reason: DynamicPET/qSlicerDynamicPETModuleWidget.cxx:22185-22205 constructs the deterministic patient/method/model/field filename using `"%1_PMAP_%2_%3_%4.dcm"`; lines 22227-22235 pass it to the Python exporter without an existence confirmation. Lines 10715-10718 say `        if os.path.isfile(output_path):` / `            os.remove(output_path)` / `        pm.save_as(output_path, enforce_file_format=True)`. A repeated export or a different study with the same patient name can silently destroy a previous map, even if the following write fails. Prompt for replacement and use safe transactional writes.

gemini.reason: Checked DynamicPET/qSlicerDynamicPETModuleWidget.cxx lines 10713-10718 and 22185-22205. When exporting a DICOM Parametric Map to the user-chosen `outputDirectory`, `outputPath` is constructed deterministically as `%1_PMAP_%2_%3_%4.dcm` (patient name, method, model, field), and `DPE_export_parametric_map` removes `output_path` if `os.path.isfile(output_path)` before calling `pm.save_as(output_path, enforce_file_format=True)`. Overwriting an earlier export with the same deterministic name in the same output directory without prompting (or before writing a temp file) is an ordinary usability/robustness concern rather than a blocking safety vulnerability.

items.title: Parametric-map export installs highdicom without consent

findings.title: Parametric-map export installs highdicom without consent
findings.explanation: On parametric-map export, DPE_export_parametric_map calls this function; if highdicom is absent it downloads and installs a package into Slicer's shared Python environment without asking, even though the user selected an export rather than a package installation.
findings.suggestion: Explain the dependency and request confirmation before installing it, as the Excel dependency helper does; handle missing dependencies without altering existing bundled packages.

gpt.reason: DynamicPET/qSlicerDynamicPETModuleWidget.cxx:9918-9919 calls `        hd = DPE_get_highdicom()` when exporting a parametric map. If the top-level package is absent, lines 9242-9254 execute `            slicer.util.pip_install("--no-deps highdicom")` without asking. This changes Slicer's shared Python environment during export; `--no-deps` limits dependency changes but does not provide consent. Ask before installation or use an appropriate dependency mechanism.

gemini.reason: Checked DynamicPET/qSlicerDynamicPETModuleWidget.cxx lines 9233-9260. Unlike `DPE_prepare_excel_dependencies` (lines 9200-9213), which prompts the user with `slicer.util.confirmYesNoDisplay` before calling `slicer.util.pip_install`, `DPE_get_highdicom()` immediately calls `slicer.util.pip_install("--no-deps highdicom")` when `import highdicom` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`. Because this only happens on user-initiated DICOM Parametric Map export (not at startup/import) and uses `--no-deps` for a small pure-Python package so existing packages cannot be upgraded or downgraded, the impact on Slicer's environment is minor, though prompting for confirmation like the Excel helper does would be better.

findings.title: Empty KIT_TEST_SRCS in DynamicPET/Testing/Cxx/CMakeLists.txt
findings.explanation: In `DynamicPET/Testing/Cxx/CMakeLists.txt`, `KIT_TEST_SRCS` is empty (the test source is commented out), which is then passed to `slicerMacroConfigureModuleCxxTestDriver`. Depending on the CMake/Slicer version, configuring a Cxx test driver with no test sources may fail or produce an empty test executable when `BUILD_TESTING` is enabled.
findings.suggestion: Either add a basic module test source file or guard `add_subdirectory(Testing)` / `slicerMacroConfigureModuleCxxTestDriver` until C++ tests are enabled.

findings.title: No enabled C++ module tests in the visible test configuration
findings.explanation: The visible test driver has no enabled module test source, so this checkout does not provide automated regression coverage for the main PET workflow through this test configuration.
findings.suggestion: Add reproducible tests for representative PET timing, fitting, and export workflows.

items.title: Placeholder metadata and "Examples" category in qSlicerDynamicPETModule.cxx

findings.title: Placeholder metadata and "Examples" category in qSlicerDynamicPETModule.cxx
findings.explanation: `qSlicerDynamicPETModule.cxx` still has the cookiecutter template strings for `helpText()`, `acknowledgementText()` ("NIH grant NXNNXXNNNNNN-NNXN"), `contributors()` ("John Doe (AnyWare Corp.)"), and `categories()` ("Examples", whereas `CMakeLists.txt` and the catalog entry use "Quantification"). Users will look for the module under "Quantification" in Slicer's module selector, not "Examples".
findings.suggestion: Update `categories()` to return `"Quantification"` (matching the catalog entry and top-level `CMakeLists.txt`), and replace the placeholder help text, acknowledgements, and contributor name (`John Doe`) in `qSlicerDynamicPETModule.cxx`.

items.title: Unprompted pip install of highdicom during Parametric Map export

findings.title: Unprompted pip install of highdicom during Parametric Map export
findings.evidence:
try:
            slicer.util.pip_install("--no-deps highdicom")
            importlib.invalidate_caches()
            import highdicom as hd
findings.explanation: When a user exports a DICOM Parametric Map (`DPE_export_parametric_map`), `DPE_get_highdicom()` runs `slicer.util.pip_install("--no-deps highdicom")` without asking the user for confirmation first (unlike `DPE_prepare_excel_dependencies`, which prompts via `slicer.util.confirmYesNoDisplay`). Additionally, because `--no-deps` is used, if any of `highdicom`'s non-bundled dependencies (such as `pyjpegls` or newer `pillow`/`numpy` requirements depending on the PyPI release) are absent, importing or using `highdicom` may fail at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Prompt the user with `slicer.util.confirmYesNoDisplay` before installing `highdicom` into Slicer's shared Python environment, just as `DPE_prepare_excel_dependencies` does for `pandas`/`openpyxl`/`xlsxwriter`.

items.title: Extension uses three Git submodules (KMAP-CPP, dPETImporter, dRTImporter)

findings.title: Extension uses three Git submodules (KMAP-CPP, dPETImporter, dRTImporter)
findings.explanation: The extension relies on three Git submodules (`KMAP-CPP`, `dPETImporter`, `dRTImporter` declared in `.gitmodules` and added via `add_subdirectory` in `CMakeLists.txt`). While Slicer's extension build system initializes submodules recursively during builds, the contents of those three external repositories are not present in this repository checkout and could not be directly inspected here.
findings.suggestion: Verify that the pinned submodule commits in `KMAP-CPP`, `dPETImporter`, and `dRTImporter` exist on GitHub and carry compatible license files.

The submodule sources listed in .gitmodules:1-9 and the exact checkout revision could not be independently verified with the available tools.

gemini.reason: Checked the safety findings raised in D1 and D2 (DynamicPET/qSlicerDynamicPETModuleWidget.cxx lines 9291-9313, 10713-10718, 22185-22205, 25647-25849). There is no malicious behavior, unauthorized data transmission, unsafe deserialization, or arbitrary file destruction; overwriting previously exported files in a user-selected export folder when the user clicks Save/Export is a minor UX/soundness issue, so safety is `ok`.
